features.title: CBD coastal strip and escarpment
features.description: The report describes a low coastal strip about 100 m wide in the north and south, widening to about 250 m / three blocks in the centre, backed by the Top Town plateau. The illustration has contours and spot labels; its elevation datum and accuracy are not supplied.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Traffic circulation
features.description: Congested CBD approaches; narrow streets conflict with pedestrians; buses lack defined routes, standing areas and discipline; uncontrolled parking/loading and one-way circulation; unresolved circulation around Independence Park.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Pedestrian environment
features.description: Broken and incomplete footpaths and abrupt ends to waterfront access beyond the CBD core.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Transit connections
features.description: Limited small-boat access and connections to ferry/liner wharfs; limited bus stops and parking around Independence Park.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Shade and green space
features.description: Limited street trees and few shade trees in the waterfront park near the market.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Vacant land
features.description: Demolitions left gaps in the urban fabric. This is the report’s 2025 observation, not a current vacancy inventory.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Line A — northern disturbance
features.description: The report associates northern Line A with landslides in unconsolidated volcanic material. Its diagram is provisional and the report says geotechnical work was ongoing in 2025. This imported trace is not a surveyed fault or a current safety determination.
features.spatialBasis: Digitised from indicative source diagram; not cadastral or survey geometry

features.title: Line B — CBD disturbance
features.description: The report describes differential settlement and damage along Line B through the former petrol station, Mamas Market and National Bank sites. Its provisional concept keeps affected properties as open space. No buildability decision is inferred; the PDF’s terminology is retained with its preliminary context.
features.spatialBasis: Digitised from indicative source diagram; not cadastral or survey geometry

features.title: Earthquake and recovery context
features.description: 17 December 2024 earthquake. Page 10 reports 14 fatalities, at least 80,000 people affected across Vanuatu, USD 197 million estimated direct damage (about 17% of 2023 GDP), an estimated 245 houses and 200 CBD businesses partially or fully destroyed and 900 jobs lost. These have different geographies, sources and reporting dates. They are not per-site attributes.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Demolition totals and source inconsistency
features.description: Page 7 says 25 buildings were demolished; page 10 says 25 require demolition, with 20 completed at the report date. Preserve this discrepancy rather than treating either as a current complete site count. Diagram sites are not a comprehensive building inventory.
features.spatialBasis: CBD-wide; no site geometry supplied

features.title: Compact urban growth
features.description: The report identifies peripheral sprawl, informal settlement growth and infrastructure pressure, and argues for compact redevelopment of the CBD. Its regional map locates the airport, CBD, wharfs, Fatumaru Bay and Erakor Lagoon, but supplies no informal-settlement polygons.
